_comment: RIGHTBREED v4 — G4 flooring risk gate. DRAFT, PENDING VET SIGN-OFF.
Mechanism: van Hagen MA et al. (2005), Am J Vet Res, PMID 15757132 — slippery
pre-weaning flooring measured a 1.6x risk of developing clinical hip dysplasia
signs (n=1733 Boxers). Four tiers, not three, because the original 3-tier
version put a plain-hip-dysplasia Labrador in the same HIGH bucket as a
Shih Tzu with BOTH hip dysplasia and IVDD — real signal was being thrown
away. VERY_HIGH is reserved for genuine compounding risk: either two
documented conditions at once, or hip dysplasia in an XL/giant breed where
more body mass mechanically worsens the same joint-slip mechanism, not
just a correlated trait. MEDIUM covers conditions with a real but weaker
connection to slippery floors specifically — IVDD's better-established
driver is jumping/obesity, not floor slip, and patellar luxation is
primarily conformational rather than floor-triggered.
OPEN QUESTION for the vets: confirm the VERY_HIGH tier split — Shih Tzu,
French Bulldog (compounding hip+IVDD), Rottweiler, Great Dane, Saint
Bernard (XL/giant + hip dysplasia, mass-amplified). Also confirm Beagle
and Dachshund (IVDD-only, no hip flag) belong in MEDIUM rather than HIGH.
Every breed in breeds.json must appear in `breeds` or the build FAILS
(scripts/validate-data.mjs). Multipliers apply to the base score:
final = base x G1 x G2 x G3 x G4. Gate only bites on hard/slippery floors —
a breed with High or Very High concern on carpet/rugs scores the same as Low concern.

classReasons.LOW: no documented joint or spinal predisposition
classReasons.MEDIUM: a real but less floor-specific condition — IVDD (jumping/obesity better-established as the driver) or patellar luxation (largely conformational)
classReasons.HIGH: documented hip/elbow dysplasia alone, ordinary build — slippery floors are a demonstrated risk factor
classReasons.VERY_HIGH: compounding risk — either hip dysplasia plus IVDD together, or hip dysplasia in an XL/giant breed where extra body mass mechanically worsens the same joint-slip risk
